sanskrit_verse:
सत्कृत्य भिक्षवे भिक्षा दातव्या सव्रताय च ।
भोजयेच् चागतान् काले सखिसंबन्धिबान्धवान् ॥
transliteration: satkṛtya bhikṣave bhikṣā dātavyā savratāya ca / bhojayec cāgatān kāle sakhisaṃbandhibāndhavān //
sph_interpretive_translation: Food must be offered with respect to the monk who observes vows; guests, friends, relatives, and associates must be fed at the proper time.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority through observance of vow-bound discipline
Causation via timely and conscious offering
Capacity-based responsibility rooted in relational duty
Consciousness alignment by honoring spiritual and social bonds
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent observes vow-bound discipline THEN community SHALL offer sustenance first
IF guest arrives within proper time THEN host SHALL provide meal without request
IF individual is friend, relative, or associate THEN feeding SHALL occur automatically upon arrival
IF sustenance is withheld from vow-keeper or guest THEN system SHALL initiate restorative completion protocol
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating disputes involving neglect of hospitality duties, the court shall recognize precedence of vow-observant individuals and relational obligations. Responsibility thresholds are determined by proximity of relationship and timeliness of offering, not intent. Retribution is replaced by mandatory restoration of feeding cycle.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through visible adherence to vows and relational proximity. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential neglect leading to breakdown of dharmic order. Responsibility is proportional to capacity of hosting, not punitive in nature. The real rule is that consciousness falters when hospitality ceases, thus restoration precedes judgment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Host must perform full meal offering to neglected guest or vow-keeper until energetic balance is restored
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Host publicly acknowledges failure and commits to future observance
Capacity Restoration: Community provides resources to ensure future compliance with feeding duties
Integrity Reintegration: Mediated sharing of meal in presence of witnesses to reaffirm dharmic bond
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands executed. Dharma is restored through right offering. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
